title: Forming the Memphis Five; Jimmy Lytell, Roth, and Durante's Alamo band
summary: After Columbia he went into artist representation and picked up the Memphis Five. They sort out Jimmy Lytell from the actor Bert Lytell, the drummer who later worked with Durante, and Durante's Alamo jazz band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, you were associated with a lot of jazz music after that. What was the next jazz band that you worked with?

Well, when I left Columbia, I went to the artist representation field, and I made records for many of the companies beside the big two, and I picked up the Memphis Five with Philly Napoleon and Mip Mole and Frankie Signorelli and the clarinet... Lytel with them? Bert Lytel. That was the trumpet. What is Bert's right name? Jimmy. Jimmy Lytel. Jimmy Lytel. Bert was the actor.
The drummer was... Was he Roth, the first drummer?
Roth, who is now with Jimmy Durante and has been with Jimmy Durante for many, many years.
Well, now Jimmy Durante had a jazz band. Was that at the same time? Was Jimmy Durante active in the period of the Memphis Five?
Well, Jimmy Durante, I think... Didn't he have this jazz band down in this place that he... The silver slipper that he and...
And earlier, a place called the Alamo, I think. Remember the Alamo? Which was far up north, uptown.
Jimmy Durante uptown? Yeah. May have been.
I think Kush has mentioned the Alamo as a place where he played with Durante and Baquet, and he thought that they were considerably imitative of the original New Orleans jazz band.
I should say it would be. The Memphis Five, when you got them, had they recorded before? Do you think that...
